 YouTube TV vs. Xfinity TV: Prices, Packages and Channels Compared
 By
 Raymond McCain 
 on
 October 18, 2026 
 in 
 All News , News 
 The right live TV service can make a big difference in your monthly entertainment budget. However, choosing between YouTube TV and Comcast Xfinity isn’t just about finding the cheapest package. It’s about getting the channels you actually watch without paying for a pile of extras you rarely use.
 YouTube TV takes a streaming-first approach, giving subscribers access to live TV, local channels, sports, and entertainment without a traditional cable box. Meanwhile, Xfinity combines its traditional TV experience with a 4K set-top box, voice remote, DVR service, and the Xfinity Stream app.
 Both services have plenty to offer, but their prices, package options, and included features differ considerably. Xfinity also offers several tiers, so comparing its entry-level package with YouTube TV’s full lineup wouldn’t tell the whole story.
 Here’s how YouTube TV and Xfinity compare in 2026, including their packages, sports coverage, DVR features, and the details to check before signing up.
 YouTube TV vs. Xfinity at a Glance
 Feature YouTube TV Comcast Xfinity TV 
 Starting price $54.99/mo. for select genre-based plans $65/mo. for TV Core 
 Comprehensive TV package $82.99/mo. for the main plan $105/mo. for TV Plus or $135/mo. for TV Premium 
 Channel lineup 100+ channels on the main plan 10+ to 185+ channels, depending on package 
 Local channels Included, subject to local availability Included, subject to local availability 
 DVR Unlimited cloud DVR 150 or 300 hours, depending on plan 
 Sports features Multiview, key plays, and sports add-ons Multiview, Fan View, sports add-ons, and voice search 
 ESPN Unlimited Included with the main plan and eligible sports-inclusive plans Included with several higher-tier packages 
 Peacock Premium Separate subscription Included with Sports & News TV and World Soccer Ticket 
 Equipment No traditional cable box required First 4K TV box and voice remote included 
 Internet Requires an internet connection Available plans and viewing options depend on your location and service setup 
 Contracts Cancel anytime Advertised as no-contract TV service 
 Prices are monthly advertised rates before applicable promotions and optional add-ons. Xfinity pricing, equipment charges, taxes, and available channels can depend on the package and location. YouTube TV’s genre-based plans have different channel lineups and prices. 
 For viewers who want a broad channel lineup without cable equipment, YouTube TV is an attractive alternative. On the other hand, Xfinity may appeal to households that want a traditional TV guide, a physical remote, and streaming apps integrated into one entertainment system.
 What You Get With YouTube TV
 YouTube TV is built for viewers who want live television without committing to a traditional cable setup. You sign up online, install the app on a supported device, and start watching through your internet connection.
 The service also expanded its package lineup in 2026, so the main plan isn’t your only option anymore.
 YouTube TV packages and pricing
 Here are the main plans and their standard monthly prices. Introductory promotions may lower the price for eligible new subscribers.
 Package Monthly price What it’s for 
 YouTube TV $82.99 100+ channels covering sports, news, entertainment, and local TV 
 Sports $64.99 30+ channels focused on live sports, analysis, and local broadcasts 
 Entertainment $54.99 50+ channels focused on entertainment and lifestyle programming 
 News + Entertainment $62.99 70+ channels combining news and entertainment 
 Sports + News $71.99 50+ channels focused on live sports and news 
 Sports + Entertainment $71.99 70+ channel lineup with a combination of sports and entertainment channels 
 News + Entertainment + Family $69.99 80+ channels focused on news, entertainment, and family programming 
 Sports + Entertainment + Family $77.99 90+ channels focused on sports and entertainment with family channels 
 YouTube TV also offers additional options and paid add-ons, including its 4K Plus add-on ($9.99/mo.). Check the official YouTube TV plans page for the latest lineup and availability.
 For households that watch a little of everything, the main YouTube TV plan remains the most comprehensive option. However, someone who mainly watches sports or entertainment may save money by choosing a genre-based package instead.
 Why YouTube TV stands out
 The biggest selling point is convenience. You don’t need a traditional cable box, a technician appointment, or a dedicated TV connection to get started.
 Instead, YouTube TV works through supported smart TVs and streaming devices, including Apple TV, Google TV, Roku and Amazon Fire TV, as well as compatible phones, tablets, and computers.
 Subscribers also get several useful features:
 Unlimited cloud DVR: Record as many programs as you like, with recordings generally available for up to nine months.
 Six household accounts: Each member can have a separate profile, recommendations, and DVR library.
 Three simultaneous streams: Watch on up to three devices at once under the standard home-streaming allowance.
 Multiview: Watch up to four live feeds on one screen, an appealing option for sports fans following multiple games.
 Optional add-ons: Add services or features such as NFL Sunday Ticket, NFL RedZone with Sports Plus, and 4K Plus for an additional charge.
 YouTube TV also introduced fully customizable Multiview , giving viewers more control over which eligible live feeds appear together.
 For sports fans, ESPN Unlimited is another significant addition. Eligible subscribers to the main YouTube TV plan and sports-inclusive plans can access ESPN Unlimited content within the YouTube TV experience. The programming includes additional live events and digital sports coverage beyond traditional linear channels.
 However, don’t assume every ESPN program is included in the same way. As Cord Cutters News reported in September , certain programming remains subject to rights restrictions.
 A YouTube TV deal worth considering
 YouTube TV currently has an introductory offer for eligible new subscribers that lowers the price of its main plan to $67.99 per month for the first five months after a free trial. That’s $15 off the standard monthly price, adding up to $75 in savings.
 The deal ends November 26, 2026. After the promotional period, the price increases to $82.99 per month unless the service changes its pricing or you cancel.
 Check the YouTube TV offer and sign up here. 
 The promotion is worth considering if you want a full live TV lineup for football season, fall shows, and the holiday viewing season. Just remember to budget for the regular rate after the first five months.
 What You Get With Comcast Xfinity TV
 Xfinity takes a different approach. Instead of relying entirely on an app-based subscription, its TV service centers on the X1 platform, which combines live television, on-demand programming, DVR recordings, and supported streaming apps.
 The service also has several packages, ranging from a relatively small selection of local and national networks to a much broader lineup with additional sports and entertainment channels.
 Xfinity TV packages and pricing
 Xfinity’s current national TV lineup includes five main options. Here’s how they compare based on the company’s X1 TV package information .
 Package Monthly price Channel lineup DVR storage 
 TV Core $65 10+ channels 150 hours 
 Sports & News TV $90 50+ channels 300 hours 
 World Soccer Ticket $95 55+ channels 300 hours 
 TV Plus $105 125+ channels 300 hours 
 TV Premium $135 185+ channels 300 hours 
 All five packages include a first 4K TV box and voice remote. Xfinity advertises the plans without long-term contracts, and eligible customers may qualify for a monthly discount by bundling TV with Xfinity Internet.
 Keep the fine print in mind: Xfinity’s advertised TV prices don’t necessarily represent your entire household bill. Taxes and additional equipment may cost extra, and the channels and offers available to you can depend on your service address. Confirm the final price before ordering.
 For a closer look at the company’s updated packages, see our coverage of Xfinity’s new video plans and pricing .
 Why Xfinity might be worth the money
 Xfinity’s appeal comes down to its traditional TV experience and the extras included with some of its higher-tier packages. For example, the Sports & News TV package includes Peacock Premium and ESPN Unlimited. That gives sports fans access to a mix of live games, traditional sports networks, and streaming-exclusive programming without purchasing those two services separately.
 Meanwhile, TV Premium adds regional sports networks in supported markets, making it worth investigating if you follow a local professional team.
 Here are some of Xfinity’s biggest advantages:
 A physical TV box and voice remote: The X1 interface is familiar to people who prefer traditional channel surfing rather than navigating an app.
 A larger DVR allowance on higher tiers: Sports & News TV, World Soccer Ticket, TV Plus, and TV Premium include 300 hours of DVR storage.
 Multiview and Fan View: Watch up to four live games simultaneously, while Fan View puts scores, statistics, and other information within reach.
 Peacock Premium included with select packages: Sports & News TV and World Soccer Ticket include the ad-supported version of Peacock Premium.
 ESPN Unlimited access on select packages: Several higher-tier plans include the service, adding more sports content to the lineup.
 The Xfinity Stream app: Watch eligible live channels, on-demand content, and recordings on supported devices at home or on the go.
 Xfinity also offers optional sports packages. For example, its More Sports & Entertainment add-on costs $9.95 per month and includes NFL RedZone during the 2026 regular season, along with other sports channels.
 Furthermore, Xfinity’s Stream app supports a range of devices, including Amazon Fire TV, Apple TV, Roku, compatible smart TVs, phones, tablets, and web browsers. However, certain features and programming vary by device and subscription.
 Plus, the included X1 TV box supports 4K, and Xfinity makes eligible live events available in 4K at no additional charge whenever programmers provide a 4K feed. 
 For customers who already use Xfinity Internet, bundling can simplify billing and potentially reduce the monthly cost. Still, the important number is the final price for the TV and internet services you need, rather than the advertised price of TV alone.
 YouTube TV vs. Xfinity for Sports Fans
 Sports coverage deserves its own comparison because neither service automatically guarantees access to every game.
 YouTube TV’s main plan offers a broad range of national sports networks and local broadcast channels. Its sports-focused package provides another option for viewers who want to concentrate on games and sports coverage without paying for as many entertainment channels.
 Subscribers can also purchase NFL Sunday Ticket separately to watch out-of-market Sunday afternoon NFL games. The package is an additional expense, and it doesn’t replace the need for access to local and nationally televised games.
 Xfinity, meanwhile, offers a more traditional combination of sports channels, its X1 experience, and bundled streaming services. Its Sports & News TV package includes ESPN, ESPN2, FS1, FS2, major broadcast networks, and Peacock Premium. Higher-tier options add more channels, while TV Premium includes regional sports networks in eligible areas.
 Here’s the main difference:
 What matters to you Better place to start 
 Watching several games at once without a cable box YouTube TV 
 An integrated TV guide, voice remote, and physical box Xfinity 
 ESPN Unlimited access without a separate subscription Compare YouTube TV’s main or sports-inclusive plans with eligible Xfinity packages 
 Peacock Premium included with TV Xfinity Sports & News TV or World Soccer Ticket 
 Access to your local team’s regional sports network Check both services’ channel lineups for your ZIP code 
 Out-of-market NFL Sunday afternoon games YouTube TV with NFL Sunday Ticket, or the eligible Xfinity offer for NFL Sunday Ticket 
 One detail matters more than the number of channels on the screen. Check whether your specific team is available before subscribing. Regional sports network carriage varies by market and package, and national sports channels don’t carry every local game.
 What to Know Before You Switch
 Before canceling cable or signing up for a new TV service, take a few minutes to review what you’re already paying for and what you actually watch.
 First, compare the channel lineups. A package with 100 channels isn’t necessarily better than one with 50 if the smaller package carries the networks you watch most often. Local ABC, CBS, FOX, and NBC affiliates are particularly important for broadcast sports, local news, and major events. Plus, you can always watch your local affiliates for free with an antenna .
 Next, consider your internet connection. YouTube TV relies on streaming, so a stable connection is essential. You can continue using Xfinity Internet with YouTube TV if that combination works for your household; switching your TV provider doesn’t automatically require you to change internet providers. However, if you are thinking about leaving Xfinity, our recent guide on home internet alternatives can help you save today .
 Also, look beyond the introductory price. YouTube TV’s five-month promotion saves $75 , but its regular rate applies after the deal expires. With Xfinity, check whether a bundle discount applies and whether taxes or additional equipment change the total.
 Finally, review your current cable bill before making a move. If you cancel Xfinity TV but keep its internet service, your internet price could change depending on your existing bundle. You should also return any rented equipment and confirm that the TV portion of your service has been removed from the account.
 For additional guidance, read our full breakdown of what to know when switching to YouTube TV from Comcast or Spectrum .
 Which Service Should You Choose?
 For most viewers who want a broad live TV lineup without a cable box, YouTube TV is the stronger place to start. Its main plan includes more than 100 channels, unlimited cloud DVR, six household accounts, and flexible streaming across supported devices. The $75 introductory savings also give eligible new subscribers a lower-cost way to try the service before paying the regular rate.
 However, Xfinity deserves a closer look if you prefer the traditional TV experience or want a package that combines live channels with services such as Peacock Premium and ESPN Unlimited. Its higher-tier packages also offer larger channel lineups and regional sports networks in supported markets.
 The deciding factor is your complete bill and the channels you can’t live without. Compare the package you would actually buy, check the availability of your local networks and sports teams, and make sure the post-promotion price fits your budget.
 Ready to compare YouTube TV for yourself? View the current offer here and see whether you qualify for five months at $67.99 per month.
